provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Revision of sss two work
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to recall key concepts from SSS 2 Government syllabus.
The students should be able to identify important theories and principles studied previously.
Introduction:
Today we will revise the fundamental topics covered in SSS 2 to prepare for our exam season.
This revision will help us refresh our memory and identify areas needing more focus.
Content:
We will review major concepts like power, authority, legitimacy, the state, democracy, and federalism.
Each concept will be explained with examples from Nigerian politics such as the relationship between federal, state and local governments.
We will discuss how these concepts apply to current Nigerian political situations.
Class activity:
Students will participate in a group quiz where they answer questions on SSS 2 topics in teams of four.
Evaluation questions:
1. Define power and give one Nigerian example.
2. Differentiate between authority and power.
3. How does the principle of federalism apply in Nigeria?
4. Explain one challenge to democracy in Nigeria.
Summary:
Today's revision has helped us consolidate our understanding of key Government concepts from SSS 2.

topics.title: Basic concepts review
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to define power, authority and legitimacy.
The students should be able to differentiate between these three concepts.
Introduction:
Building on our revision, we will examine the basic political concepts that form the foundation of Government.
These concepts are essential for understanding more complex political structures and systems.
Content:
Power is the ability to influence others' behavior, often seen in how the National Assembly can pass laws.
Authority is the legitimate right to exercise power, like when the President signs a bill into law.
Legitimacy is the acceptance of authority by the people, which can be earned through democratic elections.
In Nigeria, traditional rulers have authority based on custom rather than formal power.
Class activity:
Students will create concept maps showing the relationship between power, authority and legitimacy using Nigerian examples.
Evaluation questions:
1. Define power and give one example.
2. How does authority differ from power?
3. Explain why legitimacy is important in government.
4. Give one Nigerian example of legitimate authority.
Summary:
Understanding these basic concepts helps us analyze how political systems function in Nigeria and beyond.

topics.title: The state and nation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify the four features of a state.
The students should be able to differentiate between state and nation.
Introduction:
Last week we examined basic political concepts, and now we will focus specifically on the state and nation.
These are fundamental concepts in political science that help us understand political organization.
Content:
A state has four essential features: population, territory, government and sovereignty.
Population refers to the people within the state, like Nigeria's over 200 million people.
Territory is the defined geographical area, such as Nigeria's land borders with neighboring countries.
Government is the organized political authority that maintains order and makes decisions.
Sovereignty is the supreme authority within a territory, as Nigeria has as an independent nation.
A nation is a group of people with shared identity, language, culture or history, which may or may not form a state.
Class activity:
Students will identify the four features of Nigeria as a state and discuss whether Nigeria is also a nation.
Evaluation questions:
1. List the four features of a state.
2. Differentiate between state and nation.
3. Explain the concept of sovereignty.
4. Is Nigeria a state, a nation, or both? Justify your answer.
Summary:
Understanding the distinction between state and nation helps us analyze political organizations and conflicts worldwide.

topics.title: Democracy
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to define democracy and list its types.
The students should be able to explain the practice of democracy in Nigeria.
Introduction:
After examining the state and nation, we now turn to democracy as a system of government.
Democracy is the most widely practiced form of government in the world today.
Content:
Democracy is a system of government by the whole population or all eligible members.
Types include direct democracy where citizens vote on laws directly, like in some local government decisions.
Representative democracy involves electing officials to make decisions on behalf of the people, as in Nigeria's National Assembly.
Liberal democracy emphasizes individual rights and freedoms, protected by Nigeria's constitution.
Social democracy combines capitalist economy with social welfare programs.
In Nigeria, democracy is practiced through regular elections, multi-party system, and separation of powers.
Challenges include electoral violence, corruption, and ethnic tensions during elections.
Class activity:
Students will participate in a mock election to demonstrate the democratic process and discuss its outcomes.
Evaluation questions:
1. Define democracy and list three types.
2. Explain how democracy is practiced in Nigeria.
3. Identify two challenges to democracy in Nigeria.
4. Differentiate between direct and representative democracy.
Summary:
Democracy remains the preferred system of government globally, though its practice varies significantly between nations.

topics.title: Rule of law
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain the principles of the rule of law.
The students should be able to identify limits to the rule of law.
Introduction:
Having examined democracy, we now consider the rule of law as a fundamental principle of democratic governance.
The rule of law ensures that all citizens are equal before the law and that government power is limited.
Content:
The rule of law means that everyone including government officials must obey the law.
Key principles include supremacy of law, equality before the law, and legal certainty.
In Nigeria, this is reflected in the Constitution which is the supreme law of the land.
The principle of legality prevents arbitrary exercise of power by government officials.
However, there are limits such as during states of emergency when certain rights may be suspended.
In Nigeria, the rule of law is challenged by corruption, selective application of laws, and executive overreach.
Class activity:
Students will analyze a Nigerian news case study to identify how the rule of principle was applied or violated.
Evaluation questions:
1. Explain three principles of the rule of law.
2. How does the Nigerian Constitution uphold the rule of law?
3. Identify two limits to the rule of law.
4. Give one Nigerian example where the rule of law was challenged.
Summary:
The rule of law serves as a check on government power and protects citizens from arbitrary actions.

topics.title: Separation of powers
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain the doctrine of separation of powers.
The students should be able to identify checks and balances in Nigeria's government.
Introduction:
Following our discussion on the rule of law, we now examine separation of powers as a mechanism to limit government power.
This principle divides government functions among different branches to prevent abuse of power.
Content:
Separation of powers divides government into legislative, executive and judicial branches.
The legislature (National Assembly) makes laws, the executive (President and Ministers) implements laws, and the judiciary interprets laws.
Checks and balances ensure each branch can limit the others' power.
In Nigeria, the President can veto bills passed by the National Assembly.
The National Assembly can impeach the President for misconduct.
The Supreme Court can declare laws unconstitutional.
However, in practice, the executive branch often dominates, especially during military regimes.
Class activity:
Students will create a diagram showing how the three branches of Nigerian government check and balance each other.
Evaluation questions:
1. Explain the doctrine of separation of powers.
2. Identify the three branches of government in Nigeria.
3. Give one example of checks and balances in Nigeria.
4. How does separation of powers protect citizens' rights?
Summary:
Separation of powers remains essential for preventing concentration of power and protecting democratic governance.

topics.title: Constitutions
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to differentiate between written and unwritten constitutions.
The students should be able to explain the features of Nigeria's constitution.
Introduction:
After examining separation of powers, we now turn to constitutions as the legal foundation of government.
Constitutions establish the structure of government and define the relationship between state and citizens.
Content:
A written constitution is formally documented in a single document or set of documents, like Nigeria's 1999 Constitution.
An unwritten constitution consists of various statutes, customs, and conventions, as in the United Kingdom.
Nigeria has a rigid written constitution that requires special procedures for amendment.
The constitution establishes the federal structure of government with powers shared between federal and state levels.
It also outlines fundamental rights of citizens and procedures for changing the constitution.
Class activity:
Students will compare Nigeria's written constitution with the unwritten constitution of the United Kingdom in a table format.
Evaluation questions:
1. Differentiate between written and unwritten constitutions.
2. Explain two features of Nigeria's constitution.
3. Why is Nigeria's constitution described as rigid?
4. Give one example of a fundamental right in Nigeria's constitution.
Summary:
Constitutions serve as the supreme law of the land and provide the framework for government organization and operation.

topics.title: Federalism
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to define federalism and explain its features.
The students should be able to analyze Nigerian federalism.
Introduction:
Having studied constitutions, we now examine federalism as a system of government practiced in Nigeria.
Federalism divides power between central and regional governments, which is particularly relevant in Nigeria's diverse society.
Content:
Federalism is a system of government where power is divided between central and regional authorities.
Key features include written constitution, division of powers, and supremacy of central law in federal matters.
In Nigeria, federalism is practiced through three tiers: federal, state, and local government.
The exclusive legislative list contains areas only the federal government can legislate on.
The concurrent list contains areas both federal and state governments can legislate on.
Residual powers belong to states under the principle of devolution.
Challenges include revenue allocation, resource control, and ethnic tensions.
Class activity:
Students will debate the effectiveness of Nigerian federalism in addressing the country's diversity and challenges.
Evaluation questions:
1. Define federalism and list its features.
2. Explain the three legislative lists in Nigeria's federal system.
3. Identify two challenges to Nigerian federalism.
4. How does federalism promote national unity in Nigeria?
Summary:
Federalism remains a crucial system for managing Nigeria's diversity while maintaining national cohesion.

topics.title: Political parties
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to define political parties and list their functions.
The students should be able to differentiate between types of political parties.
Introduction:
As we approach our exam period, we examine political parties as essential organizations in democratic governance.
Parties play a crucial role in representing citizens' interests and forming governments in Nigeria's democracy.
Content:
A political party is an organization that seeks to influence government policy by winning elections and exercising political power.
Functions include recruiting political leaders, formulating policies, educating citizens, and organizing government.
Types include single-party systems where only one party is allowed, multi-party systems with several parties, and two-party systems with two dominant parties.
Nigeria operates a multi-party system with numerous parties like APC, PDP, and LP.
Party discipline ensures legislators vote according to party position, though this can sometimes undermine independent judgment.
Class activity:
Students will research and present on the history, ideology, and current influence of one major Nigerian political party.
Evaluation questions:
1. Define political party and list four functions.
2. Differentiate between single-party and multi-party systems.
3. Identify three major political parties in Nigeria.
4. Explain the importance of party discipline in governance.
Summary:
Political parties serve as essential links between citizens and government in democratic systems like Nigeria's.

topics.title: Revision and WAEC practice
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to apply knowledge to answer WAEC-style questions.
The students should be able to identify areas needing further revision.
Introduction:
As we conclude the term, we will practice with past WAEC questions to prepare for the examination.
This practice will help us become familiar with the question format and improve our exam techniques.
Content:
We will review past WAEC questions covering all topics studied this term including democracy, rule of law, separation of powers, federalism and political parties.
Questions will include definition, explanation, comparison, and analysis types requiring structured answers.
We will practice time management techniques for the examination.
Marking schemes will be provided to understand how answers are evaluated.
Common mistakes to avoid include not following instructions, poor time management, and inadequate explanations.
Class activity:
Students will complete a timed past WAEC paper under examination conditions followed by group discussion of answers.
Evaluation questions:
1. Answer two questions from the past WAEC paper provided.
2. Identify one area where you need further revision based on the practice questions.
3. Explain how you will improve your exam technique.
Summary:
Today's practice has prepared us for the WAEC examination and highlighted areas needing further attention.
